questions: Have you noticed involuntary movements or shaking of your hands, arms, head, or body?
Do these movements occur when you are sitting still?
Do they become worse when you reach for or hold something?
Do the movements improve when you are distracted or concentrating on another task?
Have the movements been gradually getting worse?
Have you noticed stiffness or slowness of your movements?
Have you had difficulty walking or keeping your balance?
Have you fallen recently?
Have you noticed weakness or loss of coordination on one side of your body?
Have you had numbness or tingling?
Have you had changes in your speech or swallowing?
Have you noticed changes in your handwriting?
Have you had changes in your sense of smell?
Have you experienced episodes of dizziness or fainting?
Have you had any recent head, neck, or limb injury?
Have you started or changed any medications before these symptoms began?
Do you use medication for nausea, psychiatric conditions, seizures, or asthma?
Does anyone in your family have tremor, Parkinson’s disease, or another movement disorder?
Do you drink alcohol, and does it temporarily reduce the movements?
Have the symptoms interfered with dressing, eating, walking, or other daily activities?
served: distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side)
entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm)
suggestibility / sham stimulus (tuning fork or vibration applied as 'treatment')
variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination
results: 1. distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side): POSITIVE - marked decrease in tremor amplitude with distraction
2. entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm): POSITIVE - the head tremor takes up the paced frequency
3. suggestibility / sham stimulus (tuning fork or vibration applied as 'treatment'): POSITIVE - vibration triggers and modulates the head and limb tremor
4. variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination: CHANGE IN TREMOR DIRECTIONALITY - specificity 0.91 for functional head tremor in the source cohort
5. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal; no cervical dystonic posturing and no sensory trick
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder with functional (psychogenic) tremor, predominantly functional head tremor, caused by abnormal involuntary nervous-system motor control rather than structural neurodegeneration

ALTERNATIVE: Essential tremor

ALTERNATIVE: Dystonic tremor

ALTERNATIVE: Parkinsonian tremor
